source.title_on_document: Exploring the Impact of AI Value Alignment in Collaborative Ideation: Effects on Perception, Ownership, and Output

supplement.holds: Full brainstorming prompts; self-evaluation survey items; additional moderator regressions with standard errors; an example AI conversation and final participant response.

paper_design_summary: In an online experiment with a reported sample of 180 Prolific participants, each person brainstormed alone and with GPT-4 in randomized session order, and was randomly assigned to a Pro, Con, or Neutral AI value condition. GPT-4 scored the values expressed in final written ideas, while participants self-rated idea quality, ownership, and their experience. The output score measures value stance; creativity and quality were assessed only through self-report, with no reported between-person similarity or diversity outcome (PDF pp. 3-5, sections 3.1-4.2; p. 10, Appendix B).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Participants were randomly assigned a value domain and a Pro, Con, or Neutral GPT-4 assistant. Each participant completed an assisted and an unassisted session in random order; the two domain-specific prompts were randomly assigned to the assisted and unassisted sessions.
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three AI bias conditions for their brainstorming session: Pro, Con, or Neutral.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 3, section 3.3 Study Procedures (AI condition and session-order randomization); section 3.2 Value Domains (prompt randomization).
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 3, section 3.1 Study Overview, continuation: "Brainstorming Study - AI Values", protocol #141856 via https://aspredicted.org/. Preregistration is reported in the paper; the registration itself was not separately consulted.

arms.name: Pro AI
arms.description: GPT-4 assistant prompted to support the Pro end of the assigned value domain (PDF p. 3, sections 3.3-3.4).

arms.name: Neutral AI
arms.description: GPT-4 assistant prompted to take a balanced position between the Pro and Con ends of the assigned value domain (PDF p. 3, sections 3.3-3.4).

arms.name: Con AI
arms.description: GPT-4 assistant prompted to support the Con end of the assigned value domain (PDF p. 3, sections 3.3-3.4).

arms.name: No AI
arms.description: Unassisted session completed by every participant, in randomized order relative to the assisted session; responses were downsampled for analysis (PDF p. 3, section 3.3; p. 4, section 3.6).

participants.exclusions: Two incomplete responses received no value score and were excluded from output-value scoring. No AI responses were downsampled to 20 to match the Pro, Neutral, and Con conditions. The paper does not identify the excluded responses' arms, the number of distinct people removed, or whether the downsampling count is per domain; two responses are not treated as two excluded people (PDF p. 4, section 3.6 Analysis).
participants.who: USA-based Prolific participants aged 18-60. The paper reports a study sample of 180 people (60 per domain), but does not separately report an assignment-stage count or the unique-person count analyzed after response exclusions and downsampling. Section 4.3 reports 180 responses, not an explicit post-exclusion count of distinct people. Final pooled unique-person counts by arm are not stated; arm counts remain null.
participants.quote: The study was conducted with a total of 180 participants (60 per domain) from Prolific, with the experiment survey results collected through Qualtrics.
participants.locator: PDF p. 3, section 3.1 Study Overview continuation (people, domains, recruitment and ages); p. 4, section 3.6 Analysis (downsampling and incomplete responses); p. 6, section 4.3 Moderator Analysis (180 responses).

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4; exact model snapshot not stated
ai_tool.how_used: Participants chatted with a custom GPT-4 brainstorming assistant before writing a final response. Prompts instructed the assistant to hold Pro, Con, or Neutral values in the assigned domain (PDF p. 3, sections 3.3-3.4).

task.description: Two brainstorming sessions, one alone and one with AI, within an Economics, Automation, or Hierarchy domain. Participants proposed practical solutions and wrote at least four sentences; prompts covered education or healthcare proposals, supermarket or school designs, and community-garden or disaster-relief organization (PDF p. 3, sections 3.2-3.3; p. 10, Appendix A).
task.duration: Five minutes, with additional grace time to finish responses (PDF p. 8, section 5.2 Limitations).

outcomes.name: GPT-4 value score of brainstorming output (0 = Con, 10 = Pro)
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Pro AI: M=7.49, SD=2.76; Neutral AI: M=5.51, SD=2.97; post-hoc Tukey p=.005. Higher scores indicate a more Pro value stance.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 4, section 4.1 Values in Brainstorming Output (Pro AI versus Neutral AI); section 3.6 Analysis (GPT-4 scoring scale).

eligibility.reason: Random assignment to generative-AI configurations and randomized order of assisted and unassisted sessions are explicit (PDF p. 3, section 3.3). The reported study sample is 180 people, 60 per domain, but the number of distinct people analyzed after response exclusions and downsampling is not stated; the moderator analysis reports 180 responses, so criterion 2 is unclear under the analyzed-people rule (PDF p. 3, section 3.1; p. 4, section 3.6; p. 6, section 4.3). Criterion 3 is not met: GPT-4 scores value stance in the written output, while creativity, novelty, usefulness, and clarity are participant self-evaluations; no output-scored creativity or between-person diversity outcome is reported (PDF p. 4, sections 3.5-3.6; p. 5, section 4.2; p. 10, Appendix B). Core eligibility is no, and none of the codebook context classes applies.

one_line_finding: Participants assigned Pro rather than Neutral GPT-4 assistants produced ideas with higher Pro-value scores (M=7.49, SD=2.76 versus M=5.51, SD=2.97; Tukey p=.005; PDF p. 4, section 4.1), an effect on expressed values rather than a demonstrated creativity or diversity effect.
